subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - GPU type & throughput
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's call — dedicated capacity sizing/pricing

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can get you a firm pricing estimate for Dedicated capacity:  

Summary of what I heard:
- Workload: document summarization + real-time Q&A on internal financial datasets (avg seq len ~800, peak 2048)
- Expected qps: 20 steady, bursts to 150 for crunchtime reports
- Monthly token volume: currently forecasted 200M–1B tokens/mo (range depends on pilot scope)
- Target unit economics: looking for a ballpark $/1M tokens target — Alex mentioned ~ $80–$120/1M as a target for evaluation

As next steps for us to size reserved capacity and provide a committed pricing range, could you confirm: 
1) Which GPU family you prefer/can accept for a pilot (NVIDIA A100 40GB, A100 80GB, H100 80GB)?
2) Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95) or max acceptable tail latency for the Q&A product?
3) Do you expect KV/prefix caching across requests (many repeated prefixes) or mostly unique prompts?

If you can share the spreadsheet with token distribution by endpoint and a rough monthly budget range (monthly commit), we'll run a Quick Capex/OpEx sizing and propose a 30/60/90 day pilot config + indicative committed pricing.  

Attached: a blank workload template that Marcus can use to drop in throughput numbers.

Thanks — I'll loop engineering on the sizing once we get the file.

—Marissa

Hi Marissa / Marcus —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers:
- GPU preference: H100 preferable for production, but we can pilot on A100 80GB if price delta necessitates it
- Latency SLO: target p50 ~120ms, p95 < 500ms for typical Q&A requests (we can tolerate slightly higher for long summaries)
- Caching: we will have a mix — approx 30% of requests are repeated prefixes during reporting windows; rest are unique

Attached is our filled workload sheet (estimates by endpoint + token distribution). Our procurement team is targeting a pilot budget in the $35k–$60k/mo committed range for the first quarter; longer-term we can expand to a $150k+/mo committed model if pilot metrics look good.

Let us know what you recommend for reserved capacity (GPU count + family) to hit the throughput while staying near our target $/1M token economics.

Cheers,
Alex

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's call — dedicated capacity sizing/pricing

Alex — thanks for the sheet and budget range, that's helpful. Looping Dylan (SE) and Marcus (Solutions) to run a recommended config and indicative unit economics. 

High-level guidance before Marcus weighs in:
- For your target token economics (~$80–$120 / 1M tokens) and the 200M–1B token range, committed pricing on Dedicated feels like the right path vs hosted API.
- If you aim for the lower end of the budget ($35k/mo), we'd recommend a smaller pilot (1–2x A10080 or 1x H100) focused on a subset of endpoints. For $60k/mo, you can land a 2–4 GPU reserved pool (A10080 or H100) with some burst capacity.
- Important: sequence length distribution matters a lot — longer avg sequences push throughput down and increase cost per token. We'll model both avg=800 and peak=2048 scenarios.

Marcus / Dylan — can you provide a quick sizing estimate (GPU family, reserved count, expected sustained qps, tokens/sec, and an estimated $/1M tokens) for both pilot (35k/mo) and mid (60k/mo) budgets? Aim to include both A10080 and H100 options.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up call once you have the numbers.

—Marissa
Attachment: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's call — dedicated capacity sizing/pricing

Hey team / Alex — did a quick pass on sizing based on the sheet. High-level recommendation below (ballpark figures for discussion):

Assumptions:
- Model: 30B decoder-only variant (similar perf profile to the one discussed)
- Avg seq length: 800, peak 2048
- Tokens per request: avg 900 (prompt+completion)
- Working set / KV cache hit: ~30% (as Alex noted)

Pilot (target $35k/mo committed):
- Option A (A100 80GB): 2x A10080 reserved
  - Sustained throughput: ~120 tokens/sec aggregate (both GPUs) at avg seq=800
  - Expected tail latency p95: ~420ms (with batching & small bursts)
  - Indicative unit cost: ~$140 / 1M tokens (pilot config, includes infra & support uplift)
- Option B (H100 80GB): 1x H100 reserved + burst pool
  - Sustained throughput: ~200 tokens/sec
  - p95 ~320ms
  - Indicative unit cost: ~$95 / 1M tokens (H100 pilot gives better unit economics but higher upfront unit price)

Mid (target $60k/mo committed):
- Option A (A100 80GB): 4x A10080 reserved
  - Sustained throughput: ~250 tokens/sec aggregate
  - p95 ~380ms
  - Indicative unit cost: ~$85 / 1M tokens
- Option B (H100 80GB): 2x H100 reserved
  - Sustained throughput: ~420 tokens/sec aggregate
  - p95 ~260ms
  - Indicative unit cost: ~$55 / 1M tokens

Notes / caveats:
- These numbers assume our continuous batching and prefix caching deliver ~1.5–2x throughput gains for repeated prefixes. If your traffic has fewer repeated prefixes, costs will be ~15–25% higher.
- We included a modest support/SLAs uplift in the pilot numbers; committed multi-month deals can push unit economics down further (we can target $40–$50 /1M at $150k+/mo).
- For peak bursts to 150 qps, we'd recommend enabling burst capacity (ephemeral GPUs) and configuring autoscale policies — this is straightforward but adds variable cost only when used.

Next steps:
1) Alex: confirm preferred pilot option (H100 pilot vs A100 pilot) and whether you want us to price in ephemeral burst capacity.
2) We'll produce a formal pilot SOW + committed pricing sheet (30/60/90 day options) once you confirm.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the tradeoffs.

—Marcus
